newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHENS METRO PROJECT IS 55PCT COMPLETED - MIN.
newsitem.headline: ATHENS METRO PROJECT IS 55PCT COMPLETED - MIN.

text.p: Attico Metro S.A., the company that has undertaken the construction and operation of the Athens metro and government officials told a news conference on Tuesday, the Athens metro project was 55 percent complete.
"About 55 percent of the project has been completed," said Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis.
The metro has been designed to originally include two lines. The addition of another two lines will be considered at a later stage, Attico Metro's president, Leonidas Kikiras said.

"The need for such a means of transportation arose as a result of an important increase in the number of vehicles in the last four decades. In 1961, the number of cars was 82,000 and today it is 1,300,000," he said.
The Athens Metro will service 450,000 people daily along with another 330,000 people who will continue to use the existing Athens train, he added.
"The total cost of the project is estimated at 2 billion ecu. Financing comes from the EU and the Greek state," he said.
An important problem in the construction of the metro has been the archaelogical findings that are discovered on a daily basis and can some times be traced back even to the Neolithic Age, he said.

"There are important infrastructure projects under way in Greece. We are all cooperating in view of the possible selection of Athens to host the Olympic Games of 2004," said Dimitris Avramopoulos, the city's Mayor.
He also said that news about the new transportation project, the tram, would be released soon.

"The tram, as is true also for the metro, will relieve Athens' heavy traffic problem. It will also be functional and environment-friendly," he added. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
